holes_found.description: UNCOVERED MONITORING-INTEGRITY BUG in the checked-in poller Step 10b window-close scan (monitor/prompts/poller.md:308-340). The script derives each prediction's close date from the coarse human-readable test_window field ('August 2026') and ignores the precise sibling field test_window_closes ('2026-08-12'). For the Aug-12 eclipse cluster the 'Month YYYY' branch parses 'August 2026' to month-END (~2026-08-30 in this runtime), which is ~18-19 days LATER than the true close. Independently reproduced: with now=2026-08-09, script daysUntil=22.0 (NOT within the 7-day imminent horizon) vs true daysUntil=3.0 (clearly imminent). Consequence: the checked-in script will NOT surface the Aug-12 window closure in IMMINENT WINDOW WATCH on time, and the Step-10b 'days past close' escalation ladder (LOW->MEDIUM->HIGH) anchors to ~Aug 30, so a dome silent-ignore beginning Aug 12 would not reach HIGH severity until ~late September — a ~6-week detection blind spot on the flagship near-term prediction the operator even built a dedicated docs/eclipse-2026/ page to track. The poller corrected its scan ad hoc this cycle by preferring test_window_closes, but the checked-in script is unfixed. NOTE: the poller's own framing ('would silently miss entries that only populate test_window_closes' via return-false) mis-states the mechanism — entries are NOT skipped (test_window is a non-empty string, so closeStr is set); they are CAUGHT but mis-dated to month-end. The fix must target date-precision precedence, not a skipped-entry filter.
holes_found.recommendation: Route a small fix to decider/tinker BEFORE the next scheduled poll (Aug 12 is 3 days out): in poller.md Step 10b, prefer test_window_closes (ISO) when present, falling back to test_window string/object only when it is absent. Add a regression test: for any entry with both fields, the scan's derived close date must equal test_window_closes. This is distinct from ISS-3039 (stale imminent flags) and should be its own issue.

ONE NEW UNCOVERED MAJOR finding: poller Step 10b close-date scan prefers coarse test_window ('August 2026' -> month-end) over precise test_window_closes ('2026-08-12'), so the Aug-12 eclipse cluster (PRED-095/TIER-1/TIER-2/TIER-3/R005) sits OUTSIDE the 7-day imminent horizon (script thinks 22d out, true 3d) and the days-past-close escalation anchors ~6 weeks late. deeper_analysis: Two independent verifications backed this audit. (1) Field shape: data/predictions.json entries[] for the eclipse cluster each carry test_window='August 2026' (string) AND test_window_closes='2026-08-12' (ISO) — the precise field exists and is correct; the bug is purely which field the scan trusts. (2) Script replay: I re-ran the exact Step 10b close-date logic from poller.md against 'August 2026' with now=2026-08-09 and got closeDate 2026-08-30, daysUntil 22.0, within-7d=false — reproducing the miss. The false-negative direction is the dangerous one for our thesis: ISS-3039's false-positive stale flags merely add noise to the watch list, whereas this bug removes a genuinely-imminent flagship prediction from the watch entirely and delays the silent-ignore escalation by weeks. Devil's-advocate on my own severity call: the poller ad-hoc-corrected this cycle and a human operator is independently tracking Aug 12 via docs/eclipse-2026/, so real-world miss risk is partially mitigated; that is why this is 'major' (a specific capability is broken) not 'critical' (no false data reaches the published site). But the mitigation is a person remembering, not the checked-in automation — so it should be fixed, not relied upon.
